title: Importing .blend using "-col" hints can cause multiple collision nodes on objects that share the same mesh.
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible - v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee]



### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 (nvidia; 550.120) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9400F CPU @ 2.90GHz (6 threads)

### Issue description

When using the *same* data (here, *cubedata*) on separate objects (in Blender), while only *one* of them has "-col" in the name ...
![Blender Outliner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1f7044e-ec53-4d55-af31-db5f80a58139)

...causes Godot to create *two* StaticBody3D structures.
![Godot Inherited Scene Tree](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d14fb44a-1d98-40e7-b3ac-b669fce4c644)

I looked at the source* (am not a C++ person) and it looks like there's a Vector called `r_collision_map` which is keyed on the `mesh`. This, I think, means if one unique mesh is in that map, then *all* others users (other nodes in other parents) will also get the colliders attached.

e.g line 881 in *
```C++
... } else if (_teststr(name, "col")) {
	_pre_gen_shape_list(mesh, shapes, false);
	r_collision_map[mesh] = shapes;
...
```
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/af2c713971499953373380b9ae8673f64423bd59/editor/import/3d/resource_importer_scene.cpp#L881

The result is that a single `Cube-col` results in two nodes in Godot with the collision nodes attached.

### Steps to reproduce

Try the MRP.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[Here](https://codeberg.org/dbat/blender-godot-col-issue)
